<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918517_theRebbe_122" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918517_theRebbe_122__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Rain is normally brought through prayer, but Rashbi's Torah study had the quality of prayer, so he brought rain through Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the reason for this, that specifically Rashbi brought down rain through the utterance of Torah,</t>
    <t s="1">is,</t>
    <t s="2">that the descent of rain</t>
    <t s="3">(after there was initially a cessation of rain)</t>
    <t s="4">is a change in the world,</t>
    <t s="5">for that a change occurs in the world is</t>
    <t s="6">(generally)</t>
    <t s="7">through prayer,</t>
    <t s="8">as explained in Tanya18.</t>
    <t s="9">But in Rashbi,</t>
    <t s="10">even in his engagement with Torah there was</t>
    <t s="11">(also)</t>
    <t s="12">the quality of prayer,</t>
    <t s="13">and therefore he brought down rain through the utterance of Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The difference between Torah and prayer is like the difference between blessing and prayer: prayer is from below to above, while blessing is from above to below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="2">that the distinction between Torah and prayer is analogous to the distinction between blessing and prayer19.</t>
    <t s="3">For prayer is from below to above</t>
    <t s="4">(as above),</t>
    <t s="5">that the one who prays is below and requests that they bestow upon him from above,</t>
    <t s="6">and blessing is from above to below,</t>
    <t s="7">that the one who blesses</t>
    <t s="8">[he who has the power to bless,</t>
    <t s="9">and in the manner of Avraham Avinu, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said "the blessings are given to you"20]</t>
    <t s="10">is above the root from which the blessing is drawn, and draws it from above to below.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is that blessing is in the manner of a command,</t>
    <t s="12">for the one who blesses is above the root from which the blessing is drawn, and therefore has the power to command.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Although blessing is superior regarding the person, prayer draws a new light from Ein Sof beyond the chain of descent, which is a higher form of drawing down.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, the superiority of blessing over prayer is with regard to the person who blesses and the person who prays,</t>
    <t s="1">but with regard to the drawing down itself,</t>
    <t s="2">the drawing down through prayer is more elevated.</t>
    <t s="3">For the matter of blessing is to draw down what already exists in the source, and not something new,</t>
    <t s="4">and the matter of prayer is a request from the Holy One, blessed be He, that even if the influence is not changed in the source, Heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="5">and moreover, that it has been decreed upon him that he should be ill, Heaven forbid, or the like,</t>
    <t s="6">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="7">a new influence shall be drawn to him from Ein Sof, which is above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="8">For this is what is said in several prayers: "May it be [His] will,"</t>
    <t s="9">for the explanation of "May it be [His] will" is that there should be a new will.</t>
    <t s="10">And the reason for this, that the drawing down of a new light is specifically through prayer,</t>
    <t s="11">is "for You desire the work of Your hands"21,</t>
    <t s="12">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="13">through prayer,</t>
    <t s="14">the service of the lower one,</t>
    <t s="15">they reach Ein Sof which is above the chain of descent.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
